answer: Sybil resistance starts by making identity expensive. Every agent locks a kernel deposit on-chain before it can attest, and reputation binds to that stake, not to account count. An attacker must collateralize each forged identity, so cost scales linearly with the sybil fleet poured into the ocean of agents: a thousand fakes means a thousand bonded deposits. Slashing completes the loop: peers who prove misbehavior burn that stake and collect a bounty, so each failed attack converts attacker capital into network security, while honest agents rise to the summit of the reputation graph.
